prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1339; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a report of a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by a third-party vehicle. Claimant reports pain in left wrist and was transported to urgent care by ambulance from the scene. Police report requested.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant confirmed she is not represented by an attorney and wishes to handle the claim directly. Explained the claims process, the bodily injury evaluation steps, and that medical records and wage documentation will be needed. Claimant states she was unable to work for several days after the collision.

Entry 3: Medical records received from urgent care. Imaging confirms a fracture of the distal radius in the left wrist. Treating physician has recommended immobilization and orthopedic follow-up. Claimant has been provided a list of in-network providers and asked to send all bills and discharge paperwork as they arrive.

Entry 4: Liability review completed. Third-party driver admitted to following too closely and not braking in time. Photographs of both vehicles and the intersection reviewed and consistent with the statements. Liability accepted at fault for the rear-end impact. Property damage estimate for the insured vehicle sent to repair shop for final inspection.

Entry 5: Claimant called to check status. Orthopedic follow-up is scheduled and claimant reports ongoing limited grip strength and difficulty with daily tasks. Reminded claimant that she may request a copy of the claim file and that she can seek independent advice at any time. Bodily injury reserve reviewed and file flagged for periodic follow-up until treatment concludes.
